system.name: Model-based unsupervised pre-training and fine-tuning (MuZero-style agent)
system.one_liner: Study of when model-based agents transfer better: pre-train by intrinsic exploration, then fine-tune on task reward while carrying over chosen components.

content.variant_note: pre-training (b) and two fine-tuning panels (c, d) redraw the same four components, next to the model diagram (a); the fine-tuning rows are a design family of what is carried over
content.argues: Which components (observation encoder, prior heads, model, dynamics heads) are carried over from a model-based or a model-free pre-trained agent is the experimental variable.
content.subject: A MuZero-style model diagram, an intrinsic-reward pre-training setup, and rows of component cells coloured by what each fine-tuning condition transfers.

lessons.what_to_learn: Show an ablation design as rows of the same component cells redrawn once per condition, with a two-colour outline code (navy = from model-based, pink = from model-free) and grey for re-initialised blocks, so the reader can read off which parts each experiment carries over.
lessons.suits: Transfer, initialisation or component-ablation studies where one modular architecture is trained under many partial-reuse settings.

evidence: Colored blocks indicate components that are transferred while gray blocks indicate those that are re-initialized.
During pre-training, the agent interacts with an environment attempting to optimize an intrinsic exploration objective.
Red indicates transfer from a pre-trained model-free agent, while blue indicates transfer from a pre-trained model-based agent.

summary: The paper studies when and why model-based agents help transfer in reinforcement learning: agents pre-trained by intrinsic exploration are fine-tuned on task rewards while different components are carried over. Figure 1 sets up the study in four lettered panels. (a) draws the model-based agent: an observation encoder, prior heads and an unrolled chain of model and dynamics heads, each step ending in a MuZero-style loss and a self-supervised SPR loss. (b) shows unsupervised pre-training of model-based and model-free agents with an RND reward. (c) and (d) redraw rows of component cells for each fine-tuning condition (MB to MB, MF to MB, OE+PH and so on), where grey cells are re-initialised and yellow cells with navy or pink outlines come from model-based or model-free pre-training.
summary_zh: 论文研究基于模型的强化学习何时、为何有利于迁移。图 1 分四个面板：(a) 模型结构与损失，(b) 内在奖励预训练，(c)(d) 用成排组件格子表示微调迁移哪些部分，灰为重新初始化，蓝、红描边黄格来自基于模型或无模型预训练。
notes: The prior listed contribution-mosaic first with design-family; here stage-pipeline (phase-bands) is primary because panels (b)-(d) draw pre-training and fine-tuning phases over shared components, and (c)-(d) are read as a design family under side-by-side-contrast. The environment frame looks like RoboDesk but the figure does not name it (the paper uses Crafter, RoboDesk and Meta-World). The digest's large 124x23 pt picture sizes do not match the small thumbnails seen in the preview and were ignored. The caption calls the navy outline 'blue'.
